source: pi-jev-model-router 0.8.0 questions and composition, unchanged as the baseline

taskKinds.plan: Deciding what to build, sequencing work, or designing an approach before editing
taskKinds.implement: Writing or changing code, scripts, or configuration to produce a concrete result
taskKinds.write: Producing prose, documentation, comments, or other non-code content from scratch
taskKinds.debug: Diagnosing a failure, error, or unexpected behavior and finding its root cause
taskKinds.refactor: Restructuring existing code without changing intended behavior
taskKinds.review: Auditing code, a diff, a document, or a plan for problems and risks
taskKinds.research: Searching, reading, and synthesizing external information or unfamiliar APIs
taskKinds.explain: Answering a question or explaining how something works
taskKinds.operate: Running commands, tooling, git, deploys, or environment setup
taskKinds.chat: Small talk, acknowledgements, or a request with no real work attached

task_kind.instructions: Which single kind of work does `request` ask for? Judge the work the user wants done, not the topic they mention. Read `conversation_excerpt` when the request is a short follow-up that only makes sense in context. Pick the closest kind even when the request is ambiguous.

complexity.instructions: How hard is `request` to do well, judged only on the work itself? Use the conversation excerpt and environment to judge scope. Ignore how much any model costs.
criteria: Trivial: one obvious step, no design decisions, answer is known or mechanical
Moderate: a few dependent steps using familiar patterns, little ambiguity
Complex: multiple files or interacting constraints, real tradeoffs to weigh
Architectural: cross-cutting design, high stakes, long horizon, easy to get subtly wrong

capability_deserved.instructions: Setting price aside entirely, how much model capability does this request deserve to get a good outcome? Judge by stakes, difficulty, and how much a stronger model would measurably improve the result.
criteria: Minimal: any fast small model answers this just as well
Standard: a competent mid-tier model is enough
High: a strong frontier model materially improves the outcome
Maximum: correctness matters more than cost; use the best available

needs_deep_reasoning.instructions: Does answering `request` well require extended multi-step reasoning (algorithm design, subtle debugging, proof, careful long-horizon planning) rather than recall, lookup, or a short direct edit?

criteria.true: The work hinges on reasoning through non-obvious steps or edge cases
criteria.false: The work is recall, lookup, formatting, or a short direct change
